rows.grounds: dative of recipient of obeisance; compound: agha-nāśana (sin-destroying) + pura-ghātaka (fortress-slayer)
dative epithet describing the deity's manifested form
repeated salutation formula; namas + te fused in form

items.question: What form and destructive powers of the deity are honored in this subsequent salutation?
premises: The salutation follows sequentially from the previous praise.
The deity is addressed as the destroyer of sin and fortresses.
The deity is addressed as having a horse and related forms.
items.inference: Therefore, obeisance is offered to the deity who destroys sin and fortresses and manifests in a horse-like form.
uncertainties: The specific referents included in 'ādi' (etc.) of hayādyarūpāya are not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Then, obeisance and salutation to you, the destroyer of sin and fortresses, who takes the form of a horse and other forms.
